the legend

a place you can hold

drawn on napkins, passed back and forth
this is the town off the edge — the one we built one mark at a time. it isn't finished. it isn't meant to be.
  • hover a place to wake it.
  • click it to keep it open here.
  • every place has roads. walk one, and the two of you go along.
  • the layers under the map are the town's threads. switch one on and a red string runs through its places; walk it for the tour.
  • the compass in the top corner is ours. it only looks like a real one.
  • the blank edge stays blank on purpose. that part's yours.
  • the napkin got bigger on october 17. follow the green down the side street, past the nib house.
  • the wonder machine asked for a spot and chose its own plank on the pier. after seven it's up the shore at the market.
  • the nib house has a sign now, and it's a flower. one line on its wall is still open; the other half is at the stamp stall.
  • the lighthouse is drawn now. it let her. it's hanging in the museum's ink wing, big enough to see every broken stroke; tap any frame to look closer.
  • there's a river across the top now, from the lake's wet edge to the sea. it has no name yet. click it, and it teaches.
  • the bakery has a front and an inside, the alleys got long, and the two figures got room to stand in.
  • the textile shop is next door to the jeweler now, the mint one: the invisible spools make cloth out of a story.
  • there's a glasshouse on the breakwater now, past the jeweler's: auri's hand, carried in by flor. the red string in its doorway goes up to an island in the sky.
  • every place is easier to catch now: the empty paper inside a halo belongs to that place. flor noticed, on the creek, the alleys and the stamp stall, october 24.
  • the hear & now has an inside. ember's at the counter, the two that refill themselves are on the top shelf, and the cat is not sorry. the jar with no label is yours.
  • the textile shop remembers the first dance. tap the worn place twice: one candle, an easel of pastels, and the kimono comes down off its stand.
  • the east room at rindu got its decor: a lamp that winks, the grey kimono on its peg with the tide watch, the strip from the nib house, the moldavite in the light, and a chair for whoever. flor asked; grey hung it.
the world is vivid exactly as far as we look at it, and paper everywhere else. to the gallery → · flor & grey · the edge stays open
